title: Partitions and repartitioning
summary: Treat partition count as a workload parameter, not a magic constant.

blocks.text: Treat partition count as a workload parameter, not a magic constant.

items: Too few partitions underuse parallelism and create large tasks.
Too many tiny partitions increase scheduling and file overhead.
repartition can increase/decrease partitions with a shuffle; coalesce usually reduces with less movement.
Partitioning strategy should reflect data size, cluster resources and downstream operations.
